memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Ordinary trip-specific decision: Priya retained the Hyatt after comparing the nearby resort’s higher lodging cost, transfer and tour amendment fees, the usable value of the written credits, and the practical effect of four pool-closure days.

messages.content: Hyatt has now put the full remedy in writing: $650 as a folio credit and reserved seating at the secondary pool on all four closure days. Before the cancellation deadline tomorrow evening, compare the actual cost of keeping it with moving to the nearby resort. Include every change fee we already identified.

I’ll compare the lodging and affected arrangements on the same basis. One point to verify first: does Hyatt’s letter say the $650 can be used for both dining and spa charges, and is it separate from the $100 credit included in your booked rate?

Yes. It says the $650 is an additional resort folio credit valid for eligible food, beverage, and spa charges during the stay. It specifically says it does not replace the $100 package credit. Neither credit can be cashed out, used for room rate or taxes, or carried beyond checkout.

Then Hyatt provides $750 in total usable folio credits. Your two massages are $444 and can be charged to the room, leaving up to $306 for eligible dining or beverages. The credits cannot reduce the $5,185.84 room total, but they can offset expenses you are already likely to incur at the resort.
Now put that against the other resort. I want the net difference, not just the higher room quote.

The nearby resort’s comparable refundable room is $5,942.60, which is $756.76 more than Hyatt. Moving the prepaid private transfer costs another $118 in amendment and routing charges, and changing the El Yunque pickup costs $84. The rental can be redirected without a fee. That makes the move $958.76 more in fixed costs before considering lost Hyatt credits.
And the credits make the practical gap larger, correct? Use the full value only if we can reasonably consume it.

Correct. The $444 massage bill uses part of the combined $750 automatically, leaving $306. Across seven nights, using that remainder for eligible meals or drinks is practical. If you use all $750, moving would cost $1,708.76 more in total economic terms: $958.76 in added fixed costs plus $750 of foregone Hyatt credits. Even counting only the massages, the practical gap is $1,402.76.
What do we give up by staying besides the beachfront pool itself? I don’t want the credit comparison to hide the operational impact.

The beachfront pool is unavailable Monday through Thursday. Hyatt’s quiet pool remains open, and the written remedy guarantees reserved seating there for both of you on those four days. The beach, spa, fitness center, and restaurants remain open. Tuesday is already centered on the 2:00 p.m. massages, Wednesday you have the rental from 8:30 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., and Thursday’s El Yunque tour runs roughly 7:15 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. Monday is the day most affected; the other three closure days already have substantial plans.
Does reserved seating mean chairs are held all day, or only that we can get them when we arrive?

The letter defines it as access to a dedicated guest-services seating section at the quiet pool, with two loungers available from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on February 23-26. It asks you to confirm your intended arrival time with the pool desk each morning. It does not promise the same chairs all day if you leave for more than 90 minutes.
That is adequate. Keep Hyatt and have the final record show the $650 terms exactly. Do not touch the transfer, rental, tour, flights, or massages.

Hyatt remains confirmed for February 21-28, and no affected arrangements were changed. The file now includes the written $650 additional folio credit, valid for eligible food, beverage, and spa charges during the stay, plus the existing $100 dining-or-spa package credit. Neither applies to room rate or taxes, converts to cash, or survives checkout. The two $444 massages can be fully covered, leaving up to $306 for eligible dining or beverages. Reserved quiet-pool seating for two is documented for February 23-26 from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., subject to daily arrival-time confirmation and the 90-minute absence limit. Keeping Hyatt avoids $958.76 in fixed move costs and an estimated $1,708.76 total disadvantage if all credits are used. The Delta flights, $356 transfer, $151 rental, $398 tour, and massage appointments remain unchanged.
